compare.intro: Match each casual form to its full form: ちゃう is てしまう (done, often by mistake), とく is ておく (done in advance) and てる is ている (going on, or already so); なきゃ, なくちゃ and ないと all mean 'have to' (from なければ, なくては, ないと); じゃない either reminds or approves ('nice, isn't it?') or is a plain 'not' (an い-adjective's 'not' is くない); でしょ asks the listener to agree, but でしょう with a falling tone is only a guess; なんか softens an example or a feeling, while って just puts a topic on the table; and かな wonders aloud, while ってば repeats a point with impatience.

forms.tag: てしまう · done (oops, or all of it)
forms.ja: おいしかったから、ケーキを二つも食べ{ちゃった}。
forms.en: It was so good that I ended up eating two pieces of cake.

forms.ja: 友だちが[泊|と]まりに来るから、ふとんを出し{とく}ね。
forms.en: A friend is coming to stay, so I'll get the futon out.

forms.ja: 姉は今、台所でクッキーを作っ{てる}よ。
forms.en: My sister is making cookies in the kitchen right now.

check.label: Which full form is it?
check.q: ^さっきから^ずっと、外で犬が（　　）。どうしたんだろう。
why: とく is ておく, doing something on purpose to get ready. A dog barking is not preparation.
さっきから ずっと: the barking started a while ago and is still going on. That is ている, short form てる.
ちゃう is てしまう, an action that ends up done. It cannot describe barking that has gone on since a while ago.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^しまった^。[間違|まちが]えて、[大事|だいじ]なメールを（　　）。
why: しまった and [間違|まちが]えて: it happened by mistake and the speaker is upset. ちゃった (てしまった) says something went wrong.
とく (ておく) is doing something on purpose, to get ready. It clashes with [間違|まちが]えて, by mistake.
とかなきゃ means 'I must do it in advance', a plan. Nobody plans to do something by mistake.
かな wonders about something you are not sure of. Here the speaker knows exactly what happened.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q:
A：^明日^、[大家|おおや]さんが[部屋|へや]を見に来るんだって。
B：え、じゃあ^今夜中に^きれいにし（　　）。
why: てる says something is going on now or is already so. 今夜中に points to a job that is still ahead.
The landlord comes tomorrow, so the room has to be clean by tonight: しなきゃ (しなければ), 'I have to'.
ちゃった says it is already done. 今夜中に, by the end of tonight, sets a deadline that is still ahead.
したかな wonders whether something was done. B is not wondering about the past; B is reacting to news about tomorrow.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q:
A：このペン、Bさんの？
B：^ううん^、（　　）。^私のは青いの^。
why: でしょ asks the listener to agree that it is B's pen. B has just said ううん.
かな wonders. B is sure: B's pen is blue.
After ううん, this じゃない is a plain 'not': it is not mine. It is not the じゃない that reminds someone.
ってば insists on a point, and after a noun it needs だ (私のだってば). Even then it would say 'it is mine', the opposite of ううん.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^[理由|りゆう]はよくわからないけど^、今日は朝から（　　）頭が重いんだよね。
why: って after 朝から would make it a topic or a quote, and neither joins to 頭が重い.
ってば comes at the end of a sentence, to repeat a point with impatience. It cannot sit in the middle here.
でしょ also comes at the end of a sentence, to ask for agreement. It cannot sit before 頭が.
The speaker does not know why, so なんか, 'somehow', softens the feeling.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: うちに follows an action that is going on. Which tile says something happened without meaning to?
drill.full: [昨日|きのう]の夜は、テレビを{見てる}うちに[寝|ね]ちゃって、気がついたら朝だった。
drill.explain: テレビを, 見てる, うちに, [寝|ね]ちゃって. 見てる (見ている) is an action going on, and うちに follows it: while I was watching TV. [寝|ね]ちゃって ([寝|ね]てしまって) says I fell asleep without meaning to.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before:
A：明日の[会議|かいぎ]の[資料|しりょう]、どこ？
B：え、
drill.hint: って quotes what B said before, and でしょ reminds A of it. Which tile is what B did in advance?
drill.full:
A：明日の[会議|かいぎ]の[資料|しりょう]、どこ？
B：え、つくえの上に{[置|お]いといた}って言ったでしょ。
drill.explain: つくえの上に, [置|お]いといた, って, 言った. [置|お]いといた ([置|お]いておいた) says B put the papers there in advance. って quotes it, and 言ったでしょ reminds A: I told you, right?

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q:
A：明日のピクニック、何か持ってきてくれる？
B：いいよ。じゃあ、おにぎり（　　）作っていこうか。
exam.explain: なんか gives one example and keeps the offer light: rice balls or something like that. って puts a topic on the table to talk about, but おにぎり here is simply the thing B will make. かな and ってば end a sentence, so they cannot come before 作っていこうか.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q:
A：この映画、こわい？
B：ううん、ぜんぜん（　　）よ。子どもでも見られるよ。
exam.explain: B says no (ううん, ぜんぜん), so a plain negative: こわくない. An い-adjective says 'not' with くない, so こわいじゃない can only be the じゃない that reminds or approves, 'it's scary, isn't it', the opposite of what B means. こわいでしょ asks A to agree that it is scary, and こわいかな wonders, which does not fit ううん, ぜんぜん.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.before:
A：あれ、シャンプーがもうないよ。
B：ごめん、昨日ぼくが
exam.full:
A：あれ、シャンプーがもうないよ。
B：ごめん、昨日ぼくが使っちゃったから今日{買っとく}ね。
exam.explain: 使っちゃった, から, 今日, 買っとく. 使っちゃった (使ってしまった) follows ぼくが: I used it all up yesterday. から gives the reason, and 今日買っとく (買っておく) is what B will do so there is shampoo again. 今日 cannot go before 使っちゃった, because 昨日 already says when it was used.

scene.ja: 家族のグループチャット
scene.intro: Tap each word in the family chat about Grandma's birthday dinner.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: 家族のチャットで、父からの質問にすぐ_返信_した。
check.explain: 返信, a reply to a message, is へんしん: 返 ヘン (return, as in 返事) and 信 シン (message). へんじん wrongly makes し voiced, へいしん stretches へん into へい, and はんしん uses a reading 返 does not have.

skill.ask: Which of her sister's requests fall on the days Yuka is staying?
skill.passage:
ゆかへ
来週の留守番、ありがとう。お願いしたいことをまとめとくね。
①ねこのごはんは、毎日朝と夜にあげて。量は袋に書いてあるとおりでいいよ。
②ベランダの花の水やりは、^月曜と木曜だけ^。毎日やると、かれちゃうから。
③ゴミは朝のうちに出しといてね。^ふつうのゴミは火曜と金曜^、^びんとかんは水曜^だよ。
④エアコンは自由に使っていいけど、出かけるときは消しといてね。
⑤何か困ったら、となりの山本さんに聞いて。私から頼んであるから。
私は25日（日）の夜に帰るよ。おみやげ買ってくるね！
姉より
skill.strategy: List the weekdays of Yuka's stay, then check each numbered request for those days only.

item.q: ゆかさんは、10月22日（木）から25日（日）まで姉の部屋に泊まる。ねこのごはんのほかに、ゆかさんがしなければならないことはどれか。
options: 木曜日に花に水をやって、金曜日にふつうのゴミを出す。
木曜日と日曜日に花に水をやって、金曜日にびんとかんを出す。
毎日花に水をやって、金曜日にふつうのゴミを出す。
木曜日に花に水をやって、水曜日にびんとかんを出す。
short: 木・日に水、金曜にびん
item.explain: Yuka stays from Thursday the 22nd to Sunday the 25th. Watering is only on Monday and Thursday (②), so she waters on Thursday. Ordinary rubbish goes out on Tuesday and Friday (③), so she puts it out on Friday. Wednesday, the day for bottles and cans, is not part of her stay.
why: Watering is only on Monday and Thursday, so not Sunday (②), and bottles and cans go out on Wednesday, not Friday (③).
② says only Monday and Thursday, and watering every day will make the flowers die.
Bottles and cans go out on Wednesday, but Yuka's stay starts on Thursday the 22nd, so there is no Wednesday in it.
